name: Ojibwe
notes: Ojibwe (Anishinaabemowin), Algonquian. PRIMARY INPUT CONTRACT: the double-vowel (Fiero) Latin orthography, the standard teaching/reference system (Nichols & Nyholm 1995; Valentine 2001), NFC. Seven vowels: three short /i a o/ and four long /iː aː oː eː/ — note /eː/ has no short counterpart and is written with the single letter ⟨e⟩ (its length is a fact about the vowel, not spelled with a doubled letter). Obstruents form fortis/lenis pairs: the lenis series ⟨b d g j z zh⟩ is phonemically voiced-or-voiceless-unaspirated depending on context ([b~p], [d~t], [ɡ~k], [dʒ~tʃ], [z~s], [ʒ~ʃ]) while the fortis series ⟨p t k ch s sh⟩ is consistently voiceless and aspirated. ⟨'⟩ is the glottal stop /ʔ/; ⟨h⟩ for /h/ is dialectal (used where some varieties instead have /ʔ/). Nasal vowels are reported for some dialects but are not consistently written in the double-vowel system and are therefore not represented here. WRITING SYSTEMS NOT COVERED: many Ojibwe communities in northern Ontario and Manitoba write with a syllabary historically developed for Cree (devised by James Evans, c. 1840) and adapted for Ojibwe (Great Lakes Algonquian syllabics also exist with limited modern use); this file does not build a syllabics inventory because a per-community, per-dialect syllabics-to-IPA chart was not available with the same confidence as the double-vowel system used here.
